ConfirmClearHistory: Clear the history? Every recorded visit, sign-in and refusal is deleted, and the block list is kept. This cannot be undone.
ConfirmLoopbackOnly: Turn on Only Through the Proxy? Everyone, at home too, reaches Jellyfin only through your Remote Access address, so apps and casting that use the server's own address stop working. Use Undo before disabling the plugin, and see Recovery in the documentation if you lose access.
ConfirmRemoveRecord: Remove the DDNS record? This server stops keeping it pointed here, and the proxy stops answering on it. Other Addresses stay. This cannot be undone.
ConfirmRemoveRecordNamed: Remove {0}? This server stops keeping it pointed here, and the proxy stops answering on it. Other Addresses stay. This cannot be undone.
ConfirmRequestCertificate: Request a new certificate now? Let's Encrypt issues one even if the current one is fine, and the current one keeps working until the new one is ready.
ConfirmResetDefaults: Reset every limit and security setting to its default? Trusted networks, the block list, country rules, other addresses, history and Dynamic DNS are kept, and nothing changes until you save.
ConfirmTrustProxy: Trust the proxy? Jellyfin adds this machine to its known proxies, turns on remote access and restarts once, with its ports unchanged. Forward only ports 80 and 443 to this server, since anyone who reaches Jellyfin's own ports directly gets past the proxy.
ConfirmUnblockCountry: Unblock {0}? Individual blocked addresses stay blocked.
ConfirmUndoTrust: Undo Trust the Proxy? Jellyfin's network settings go back to how they were, internet visitors through the proxy are turned away, and Jellyfin restarts once.

PluginDescription: Keep your DNS records pointed at your server's current public IP.
ProviderHintChangeIp: Username and Password are your ChangeIP account credentials.
ProviderHintCloudNs: Update URL is the full ClouDNS Dynamic URL for the record. Keep it secret, since anyone with it can change the record.
ProviderHintCloudflare: Set Auth email or token to the word token for a scoped API token, or to your account email for the Global API Key. Zone name is the zone, such as example.com.
ProviderHintDdnsFm: Domain is your DDNS.fm domain. Key is the update key from your DDNS.fm dashboard.
ProviderHintDdnss: Host is your DDNSS.de host. Key is your DDNSS.de update key.
ProviderHintDefault: Fill the fields required by this provider.
ProviderHintDigitalOcean: API token is a DigitalOcean API token with read and write scope. Apex domain is the domain, such as example.com.
ProviderHintDinahosting: Username and Password are your Dinahosting credentials. Fill in Domain only when the host has more than two labels.
ProviderHintDirectnic: Paste the full gateway URLs Directnic gives you for the record. Leave IPv6 gateway URL blank if you only update IPv4.
ProviderHintDnsExit2: API key is your DNSExit API key. Domain is the domain, such as example.com, and the record name is used when it is left blank.
ProviderHintDnsMadeEasy: Record ID is the numeric ID of the Dynamic DNS record. Record password is the password generated for that record.
ProviderHintDomeneshop: API token and API secret come from the Domeneshop API admin.
ProviderHintDonDominio: User is your DonDominio API user. API key is your DonDominio API key.
ProviderHintDslReports1: Username and Password are your DSLReports credentials. This protocol carries IPv4 only.
ProviderHintDuckDns: Labels are your Duck DNS subdomains, such as myhost. Token is shown at the top of duckdns.org after you sign in.
ProviderHintDynDns1: Username and Password are your account credentials for the legacy DynDNS v1 protocol. This protocol carries IPv4 only.
ProviderHintDynDns2: Username and Password are your account credentials. Server override defaults to members.dyndns.org and can point at a compatible service.
ProviderHintDynadot: DDNS password is from the domain's Dynamic DNS settings at Dynadot. Domain is optional and splits the hostname into domain and subdomain.
ProviderHintDynu: Username and Password are your Dynu credentials. Fill in Custom domain only for your own domain.
ProviderHintEasyDns: Username and API token are your easyDNS API credentials.
ProviderHintEnom: Base domain is your domain, such as example.com. Domain password is the domain's Dynamic DNS password.
ProviderHintFreeDns: FreeDNS at afraid.org. Username and Password are your afraid.org credentials, used to get the update token.
ProviderHintFreeMyIp: Domain is your freemyip domain. Token is from the link shown when you claim it.
ProviderHintGandi: Set Auth keyword to the word token for a Personal Access Token, or any other value for an API key. Domain is the domain, such as example.com.
ProviderHintGoDaddy: API key and API secret come from developer.godaddy.com/keys. Domain is the domain, such as example.com.
ProviderHintHeNet: Record is the record name. DDNS key is the key dns.he.net generates for that record.
ProviderHintHetzner: API token is a Hetzner DNS API token. DNS zone is the domain, such as example.com.
ProviderHintHosting1984: API key is the FreeDNS API key in your 1984 Hosting account.
ProviderHintInfomaniak: Username and Password are the dynamic DNS credentials you create in the Infomaniak Manager.
ProviderHintInwx: Username and Password are your INWX DynDNS account. INWX works out the host from the account.
ProviderHintIonos: API key is your IONOS API key, in the form prefix.secret.
ProviderHintKeySystems: Password is the record's dynamic DNS password from the Key-Systems panel.
ProviderHintMythicDyn: Username is your Mythic Beasts dynamic DNS API key. Password is its secret.
ProviderHintNamecheap: Domain is your domain, such as example.com. DDNS password is from Advanced DNS after you turn on Dynamic DNS.
ProviderHintNfsn: Member login is your NFSN member login and API key comes from Profile, then API. This protocol carries IPv4 only.
ProviderHintNjalla: DDNS key is the dynamic DNS key Njalla shows for the record.
ProviderHintNoIp: Username is your No-IP username or email. A DDNS key is safer than your account password.
ProviderHintNs1: API key is your NS1 API key. Zone is optional and is taken from the record name when left blank.
ProviderHintOvh: Username and Password are your OVH DynHost credentials. DynHost carries IPv4 only.
ProviderHintPorkbun: API key starts with pk1_ and Secret API key starts with sk1_. Root domain is optional.
ProviderHintRegfishDe: Update token is the regfish DDNS token for the record.
ProviderHintSimplyCom: Account name is your Simply.com account number and API key is your Simply.com API key. Zone is optional.
ProviderHintSitelutions: Record ID is the numeric ID from your Sitelutions Recordbook. Account email and Account password are your sign-in.
ProviderHintSpaceship: API key and API secret come from the Spaceship API Manager. Domain is the domain, such as example.com.
ProviderHintYandex: Yandex has retired the legacy PDD API, so updates are expected to fail. Move the domain to another provider.
ProviderHintZoneEdit1: Username is your ZoneEdit username and DDNS token is your ZoneEdit dynamic DNS token. Zone is optional.

TaskRefreshCertificateDescription: Requests a Let's Encrypt certificate when one is missing, no longer covers your addresses or expires within 30 days, and reloads or replaces other certificates as needed.
TaskRefreshLocationsDescription: Downloads the newest DB-IP location database, used for the Dashboard's map and the country rules.
TaskUpdateDdnsDescription: Finds the server's public IP and updates each DDNS record that points somewhere else.
TaskVerifyExternalAccessDescription: Asks a few places on the internet to connect to your public address on port 443, and writes an error to the activity log when none can.
TextBlockedByRange: Blocked by a range under Advanced.
TextLimitedToken: Use the most limited token your provider allows.
TextNeverBlocked: Your network and trusted networks are never blocked.
TitleClearSaved: Remove the saved value when saved
WarningEveryoneLocal: Most visitors in the last hour came from one local address, so something in front of the proxy, such as rootless Docker or a tunnel, may be hiding their real addresses. Bans, the block list and country rules cannot work until those addresses reach the proxy.
WarningJellyfinExposed: This server also has the public address {0}, where Jellyfin's own port {1} answers without the proxy's protection. Block Jellyfin's ports for the internet in this machine's firewall.
WarningUpdateRunning: An update is already running, so this run was skipped.
